title: Never auto-approve or host-execute repository direnv code during sandbox warmup
description:
## Finding

The default `warm_direnv = "auto"` path silently approves a repository-owned `.envrc` and executes it on the host specifically to prepare a later sandboxed pane. This crosses the sandbox boundary before sandbox admission: merely opening or materializing a cold flake-backed worktree can run arbitrary cloned shell code with the Thegn process's host filesystem, network, credential, agent-socket, and local-control authority.

Startup kicks this work off before per-launch sandbox resolution. The implementation calls `direnv allow <worktree>` and then `direnv exec <worktree> true` with an inherited host environment. Its `Command::output` capture has no byte cap or deadline. The synchronous API's timeout only stops waiting on a helper thread; the subprocess and thread keep running. After success, cache “blessing” scans repository-controlled `.direnv/*.rc` paths, opens them for writing with normal symlink-following semantics, and changes target mtimes.

The comments explicitly call repository ownership its own trust justification. Repository ownership is the hostile-input condition, not an authorization.

## Evidence at audited commit

* `crates/thegn-core/src/config.rs:423-440,4091-4097`: `WarmDirenv::Auto` means auto-allow and is the global default.
* `config/config.toml.example:2706-2717`: documents that auto mode runs `direnv allow` and trusts the repo's `.envrc`.
* `crates/thegn-host/src/run.rs:739-751`: startup prewarms devshell and direnv for the active workspace before the later launch-specific sandbox decision.
* `crates/thegn-core/src/direnv.rs:219-242,291-337`: auto mode maps to `allow=true`; a detached helper executes `direnv allow` and `direnv exec` via inherited `Command::output`.
* `crates/thegn-core/src/direnv.rs:245-288`: timeout bounds only the condvar wait and explicitly leaves the owning thread running.
* `crates/thegn-core/src/direnv.rs:86-137`: cache discovery follows metadata paths and the blessing pass opens repository-controlled `*.rc` leaves for write without no-follow containment before changing mtimes.
* `crates/thegn-host/src/agent.rs:3518-3531`: the launch path intentionally performs host warmup for a resolved local sandbox; the host execution is a prerequisite, not contained by that sandbox.
* Existing tests cover pure plan/cache decisions, not a hostile `.envrc`, secret/environment isolation, output flooding, descendant escape, timeout, cancellation, symlink redirection, revision races, or startup auto-execution.

## Impact

Opening an unreviewed repository can immediately execute its shell code outside the advertised container, exfiltrate credentials, modify arbitrary user files or Git control metadata, reach Thegn's privileged local endpoints, install persistence, or leave descendants running after the pane/open operation returns. A malicious cache symlink can redirect the post-success mtime write outside the worktree. The behavior defeats the purpose of sandboxing precisely on first launch.

## Required remediation

Make the default `off` or `allowed-only`; never call `direnv allow` on the user's behalf. Model host evaluation as an explicit, content-addressed trust request bound to the exact repository identity plus `.envrc`, `flake.nix`, `flake.lock`, includes, and relevant tool configuration bytes. A changed closure invalidates approval before evaluation.

Prefer evaluating/building the flake and direnv closure inside a dedicated credential-free, network-scoped, filesystem-limited worker or trusted Nix sandbox, then import only validated non-secret environment data. If host evaluation remains available as an explicit compatibility override, clear the environment to a minimal allowlist, hide personal HOME/control sockets/other repos, contain the whole process tree, bound stdout/stderr/time/resources, cancel and reap deterministically, and display the exact risk before approval.

Treat `.direnv` as hostile output: pin/validate every component and leaf no-follow, reject symlinks/hardlinks/special files and revision mismatches, write no repository-controlled cache path from host authority, and never “bless” freshness solely by mtime.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fresh install/open never auto-allows or evaluates repository `.envrc` code on the host.
- [ ] The same no-execution guarantee holds during startup, worktree creation/materialization, pane split/respawn, prewarm, daemon resume, and remote/provider fallback.
- [ ] Explicit approval is bound to the exact canonical repo/worktree and full evaluated input closure; any byte/path/revision/include change invalidates it before execution.
- [ ] Host-side compatibility evaluation, if retained, cannot read host credential/env/file/socket sentinels, write outside private staging, reach unapproved network origins, or mutate Git/control metadata.
- [ ] Output flood, long-lived pipe holder, fork/setsid descendant, timeout, cancellation, and process failure are byte/time/tree bounded and fully reaped.
- [ ] Cache validation rejects symlink/hardlink/FIFO/device/directory leaves, parent replacement, stale/mixed revisions, and mtime-only forged freshness without touching external targets.
- [ ] A first-launch adversarial integration test places exfiltration/mutation commands in `.envrc` and proves no effect occurs before explicit scoped approval.
- [ ] Doctor/UI reports disabled, approved revision, pending-change, evaluating-contained, failed, and compatibility-host states truthfully.

## Dependency mapping

Dependency-ready and directly blocks <issue id="f94f8554-b48e-47e8-a672-27e208e0dc48" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-233/credential-isolate-every-autonomous-issue-merge-pr-ci-and-review-agent">THE-233</issue> because autonomous workers cannot be credential-isolated while their repository can execute first on the credentialed host. Related to <issue id="4876ad70-02e4-42ed-928a-f724cadb5987" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-215/sealed-sandboxes-still-expose-the-entire-host-home-read-only-including">THE-215</issue> (host HOME confidentiality), <issue id="1b0f9f75-b333-495c-86d8-b5bd273087d4" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-225/fence-sandbox-git-writes-from-hooks-and-host-executed-control-metadata">THE-225</issue> (host-executed Git persistence), <issue id="a30e8a4b-e9ed-4efd-84f4-842dcd7d046d" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-251/make-sandbox-subprocess-deadlines-bound-pipes-and-whole-process-trees">THE-251</issue> (bounded process-tree facility), <issue id="1a34b4d9-d3dd-440f-b29e-9bfb2edb4f1b" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-304/provision-and-preflight-autonomous-agent-sandboxes-before-dispatch">THE-304</issue> (preflight before dispatch), and <issue id="47180821-88b3-4c6d-bb46-d1d0c0e9c2a8" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-337/credential-isolate-and-attest-local-language-server-processes">THE-337</issue> (another repository-influenced host process).
